questions_and_answers.answer: In influencing change in policy, various methods can be employed in the forms of competition, engagement with state legislative and executive branches of government, and the involvement of interest groups. Specifically, when it comes to advancing the role of nurse practitioners (NPs) in Florida, these methods have been utilized to advocate for policy changes that enhance the scope of practice and autonomy for NPs.Competition is one method that can be used to influence change in policy. In the case of advancing nurse practitioners' role, competition can involve highlighting the benefits of NPs in terms of cost-effectiveness, access to care, and quality outcomes compared to other healthcare providers. By demonstrating the positive impact NPs can have on patient care and the healthcare system, competition can create pressure for policy changes that recognize and legitimize the role of NPs.Engagement with state legislative and executive branches of government is another crucial method. questions_and_answers.answer: Answer 1. Forms of Competition Interfering with APNs' Independent Practice Advanced Practice Nurses (APNs) face several forms of competition at both the state and national level that can interfere with their ability to practice independently. These include: Physician Groups: These groups often lobby against the expansion of APN scope of practice, arguing that only physicians have the necessary training to provide certain services. Insurance Companies: Some insurance companies may not recognize APNs as primary care providers, limiting their ability to practice independently. Hospital Administrations: Some hospitals may restrict the privileges of APNs due to internal policies or perceived liability issues. 2.
